gaps.sentence: He behaves as if he were ___ owner of the company.
gaps.explanation: 'The owner' — there is one owner, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: He was sent to ___ prison for armed robbery.
gaps.explanation: 'Be sent to prison' (as a prisoner) takes no article; visiting the building is 'go to the prison'.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ operation on his knee last year.
gaps.explanation: 'Operation' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an operation'.

gaps.sentence: ___ problem is that people don't recycle enough.
gaps.explanation: The problem (the one we are discussing); people in general takes no article.

gaps.sentence: I live on ___ Baker Street, near the tube station.
gaps.explanation: Street names take no article: Baker Street, Oxford Street.

gaps.sentence: ___ information you sent was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'The information you sent' — the clause defines it; information is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: We had ___ lunch at a bistro near the cathedral.
gaps.explanation: Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) take no article when used generally.
Plural general nouns and flu (illness name) take no article.
